name: APTL — Advanced Purple Team Lab
description: A local Docker-based purple-team lab for exercising human and AI red- and blue-team workflows in an intentionally vulnerable enterprise range.
floss_license_justification: APTL is distributed under the OSI-approved MIT License.
floss_license_osi_justification: The MIT License is OSI approved.
sites_https_justification: The repository, package index, and both documentation hosts use HTTPS.
english_justification: Project documentation and contribution channels use English.
repo_track_justification: The public Git repository records changes, authors, and timestamps.
repo_interim_justification: Feature branches and pull requests expose interim changes for review.
version_unique_justification: Every release has a unique PEP 440 version and Git tag.
release_notes_vulns_justification: Release notes identify user-visible fixes; no public APTL vulnerability with a CVE has been fixed to date.
test_invocation_justification: The Python suite uses pytest and the TypeScript suites use npm test.
tests_are_added_justification: Recent feature and fix pull requests include focused regression tests.
warnings_justification: Pre-commit, Ruff, Vale, strict MkDocs, TypeScript checks, and SonarCloud run in CI.
warnings_fixed_justification: Required checks must pass before protected-branch integration.
warnings_strict_justification: The project uses strict documentation builds and blocking lint, type, complexity, and new-code quality gates.
no_leaked_credentials_justification: Secret detection runs in pre-commit and CI; committed fixture credentials are intentionally public lab data.
static_analysis_justification: SonarCloud analyzes proposed releases and a blocking gate rejects new issues.
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: SonarCloud, Trivy, pip-audit, and OSV-Scanner examine common defect and vulnerability classes.
static_analysis_often_justification: Static analysis runs in the pull-request and integration-branch checks.
dynamic_analysis_justification: Property-based fuzz tests vary parser and configuration inputs; live release qualification exercises the deployed lab.
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: APTL production source is Python and TypeScript, not a memory-unsafe language.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: Pytest, Hypothesis, and Vitest execute with their assertions enabled.
general_comments: The complete passing-level assessment and evidence links are maintained at https://brad-edwards.github.io/aptl/security/openssf-best-practices/. Account-only attestations must be confirmed by the maintainer in the badge application.
